Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team is working through a short questionnaire focused on data domicile, retention and deletion for your hosted API. I attached the vendor workbook (tn-data-sq-2026.xlsx) with the specific fields we need answered. A few items on top of the sheet where we need clarity:

- Can customers pin data to a single AWS region (us-west-2 / us-east-1)? If so, what controls are available to enforce it?
- For model-generated artifacts (conversation logs, embeddings), what is the standard retention TTL and what options do you offer for shorter retention?
- Describe the deletion workflow when a customer requests a full purge — how do you handle backups / snapshots and how long might a residual copy remain?
- Where are audit logs stored and for how long? Are they ever replicated to other regions?

We're trying to map these answers to our internal controls (SOC2 evidence) and to the contract addendum we're preparing. If you can return a short response and any diagram (purge workflow) by EOD Wednesday that would keep us on track.

Hi Amira — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. I reviewed the workbook and answered the high-level fields there; below are the concise answers to your top items and I've attached a simple purge diagram (redwood-purge-diagram.png) for the backup lifecycle. Kimberly & Grace are looped in for technical and legal detail.

1) Region pinning
- Yes, customers can choose the primary data region for their tenant at provisioning time (options: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1).
- Enforcement: routing policies at the control plane + geo-fencing of object stores. Requests are routed to edge gateways in the chosen region; any cross-region replication requires a customer-configured policy or an explicit enabled Add-on.

2) Retention TTLs
- Default: 90 days for conversation transcripts and ephemeral request logs; embeddings default to 365 days.
- Options: We offer configurable TTLs down to 0 days (ephemeral-only) and custom retention SLAs as part of Dedicated/Private plans. For Hosted customers we can set tenant-level TTLs (30/90/180/365) at onboarding.

3) Purge workflow and backups
- Primary delete: when a purge is requested we remove the tenant's primary objects (KV, transcript blobs, embeddings) within the tenant region and mark the tenant as 'pending purge'.
- Snapshots/backups: we maintain incremental backups for disaster recovery. Snapshots are retained for up to 7 days in the same region by default for hosted plans; they are overwritten or garbage-collected during the purge process.
- Residual copies: in normal operations residual copies may exist for up to 7 days after a purge request in immutable backups; for accelerated purges we can run an expunge job (extra cost) to attempt earlier overwrites.

4) Audit logs
- Audit logs (configuration changes, admin actions, delete events) are stored in an append-only store in the tenant's region and retained 365 days by default. They are not replicated cross-region unless a customer enables cross-region analytics.

I'll hand off some of the technical specifics to Kimberly (kms, snapshot encryption, canonical evidence) and Grace for contract language around purge SLAs and accelerated expunge options.

Hi Amira — happy to provide the technical confirmation. Below are the specifics to populate your workbook (I called out exact fields you asked for).

Encryption & KMS:
- All customer data at rest (objects, embeddings, snapshots, audit logs) is encrypted using AES-256. For hosted tenants we use a service-managed KMS key by default (AWS KMS) scoped to the tenant's region.
- Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are available for Enterprise customers under the Dedicated/Private plan. CMKs allow customers to revoke access which effectively disables decrypt for new access — we provide guidance for key rotation.

Snapshots & backups:
- Snapshots are stored as encrypted objects in the tenant region. For hosted plans snapshots are retained 7 days by default; for Dedicated we support longer retention windows per contract.
- Snapshots are incremental and immutable; upon a purge request we schedule an expunge job that deletes snapshot manifests and overwrites object pointers. Physical object deletion from object storage depends on the storage provider's lifecycle (S3 object deletion is immediate once objects are unreferenced, subject to eventual object store consistency).

Purge / expunge mechanics:
- Normal purge: primary objects are deleted and metadata marked; manifests referencing snapshots are removed. This removes logical access within 24 hours in most cases.
- Expunge job: for customers who require faster eradication we run a prioritized expunge (audit of manifests + overwrite attempts). Due to immutable backup windows, residual blocks could remain in the underlying storage for up to the snapshot retention window unless the storage provider supports immediate zeroing (rare). We therefore provide an SLA-backed expedited expunge add-on (contract term) that reduces expected residual window to <48 hours in practice for supported providers.

Audit logs & evidence:
- Audit logs retained 365 days by default; exports (JSON/CSV) are available on request.
- Evidence package: we can generate a purge report (time-stamped manifests, expunge job run logs, object manifest deletion logs) and place it on a secure Drive link (example: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1TnSQevidence-tn-2026).

Notes on cross-region replication:
- We do not replicate tenant data cross-region by default. Cross-region replication is opt-in and documented in the tenant configuration. If enabled, deletion requires an expunge in each replicated region; that behavior is captured in the addendum.

If you'd like I can provide snippet language for the workbook's "technical evidence" field and export sample logs for a redaction-friendly example.

Regards,
Kimberly Park

Hi Amira — looping in a short legal-friendly statement you can use in your procurement workbook and the addendum draft. Please feel free to paste directly: 

"Redwood Inference agrees to delete or expunge customer data within the timeframes described in the service plan. For Hosted plans, logical deletion will complete within 24 hours and residual copies in backups may persist up to the published snapshot retention window (standard: 7 days). Expedited expunge is available as an add-on and, where contracted, Redwood will use prioritized expunge procedures to reduce residual exposure; targeted residual windows will be stated in the addendum for each storage provider supported. All deletion operations will be logged; Redwood will provide a purge evidence package on request that includes job run logs, manifest deletions, and timestamps."
